spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical work is the passage from a coarse genus-level representation count to a class-by-class statement: local conditions determine the available mass, while subconvexity prevents that mass from concentrating in only a few quadratic-form classes.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For sufficiently large, squarefree, totally positive v over a totally real field K, the cited ternary result gives representation by three squares exactly when the local conditions hold, with an ineffective threshold depending on K. More generally, a locally soluble v is represented by its genus many times, and the subconvexity estimate makes the individual classes in that genus represent v roughly equally often.
directed.conceptual_reading: The genus is a coarse local equivalence class that aggregates representation mass; an individual form class is the finer object actually sought. Subconvex error control upgrades a local-to-global total count into equidistribution across the fibers hidden by that coarse classification.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is from local solvability and genus representation counts to individual-class counts, with the relevant subconvex estimate controlling deviations from the genus average. One-class genera make the refinement invisible, whereas general fields expose it.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The stated three-square conclusion is restricted to large-norm, squarefree, totally positive inputs and is ineffective; local obstructions remain, and one-class behavior is exceptional. The unit does not give a uniform result for arbitrary v or arbitrary forms.
directed.uncertainty: The OCR damages the concrete quadratic forms, local-obstruction typography, and the exponent of the genus count, so those formulas should not be reconstructed here. The qualitative equidistribution claim and its dependence on subconvexity are clear.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The key representation is to turn an eigenfunction into a probability measure given by its normalized mass. Quantum unique ergodicity then becomes the concrete question of whether these measures forget the eigenstate and converge weakly to normalized geometric volume.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: On an arithmetic hyperbolic surface, normalized Maass or holomorphic newforms define probability measures from their squared magnitude against the invariant measure. The mass-equidistribution conjectures assert convergence to normalized volume as the Laplace eigenvalue or holomorphic weight grows. The source restricts to Hecke eigenforms and notes that this condition is essential in the holomorphic case, where powers of the discriminant form give a non-equidistributing counterexample; mass equidistribution would also imply equidistribution of zeros for the holomorphic forms.
directed.conceptual_reading: Replacing an oscillatory eigenfunction by its positive mass measure discards phase but retains spatial concentration, exactly the feature relevant to quantum localization. Hecke structure adds arithmetic rigidity that makes an otherwise inaccessible dynamical limit analyzable.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge runs from geodesic dynamics to Laplace eigenstates, then from eigenstates to probability measures, and finally from weak convergence of those measures to arithmetic L-function estimates developed in the following unit. Hecke simultaneous diagonalization selects a rigid one-dimensional eigenline for normalization.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conjecture is stated more broadly for negatively curved manifolds, but the source says theoretical evidence was confined to arithmetic cases. Hecke structure is exploited and cannot be dropped in the holomorphic formulation; the displayed counterexample blocks such a generalization.
directed.uncertainty: OCR corrupts the measure formulas, eigenvalue notation, and limits, but normalization, convergence to volume, and the holomorphic counterexample are recoverable. The unit states conjectures and consequences, not proofs.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Equidistribution is compressed into decay of every fixed test-function period, and that period is then represented by a triple-product central value. The decisive obstruction is degree six; CM structure matters because it factors that hard object into lower-degree pieces already covered by subconvexity.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For a fixed cusp-form test function, mass equidistribution is reduced to decay of its period against the varying eigenform's mass. A triple-product formula identifies the squared period, up to gamma and symmetric-square normalizing factors, with a central triple-product L-value. After factorization, the key general estimate is subconvexity for a degree-six symmetric-square twist, which the authors could not prove; for CM forms it factors further into degree-four and degree-two L-functions, and available subconvexity proves the stated mass conjectures in that special case.
directed.conceptual_reading: Testing a measure against spectral observables turns a qualitative convergence problem into scalar estimates. Factorization is not cosmetic simplification: it lowers analytic degree and moves the problem across the boundary between unavailable and available subconvex bounds.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are fixed test-function periods, triple-product central values, symmetric-square normalizers, and the CM factorization into lower-degree Euler products. The continuous spectrum is another test family that must also be controlled, though the passage sets it aside as easier.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The general degree-six subconvex estimate is explicitly unavailable, so the argument does not establish equidistribution for all forms. CM factorization is special and cannot be transferred to a generic form; GRH is stronger than needed here but is not proved.
directed.uncertainty: The period identity, powers, central-point typography, and gamma factors are OCR-damaged. Only the prose-supported equivalence, degree-six bottleneck, and special CM reduction are safe without scan verification.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The approximate functional equation identifies the real object that must improve: a smoothed coefficient sum of square-root conductor length. Convexity is what follows without cancellation, and the functional equation cannot be reused to manufacture the missing saving because it merely returns a comparable dual sum.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For a self-dual cuspidal L-function, contour shifts and the functional equation yield an approximate functional equation: the central value is represented by a rapidly smoothed sum of coefficients up to scale roughly the square root of the analytic conductor. Known average coefficient bounds give convexity. Subconvexity therefore requires cancellation in that sum, but direct control is difficult because little is known pointwise about the coefficients, and dualizing again gives a sum of the same type.
directed.conceptual_reading: The approximate functional equation is a diagnostic reduction: it spends the available symmetry to localize the central value and reveals cancellation, rather than further formal manipulation, as the remaining resource. Embedding the target in a family is proposed because the isolated coefficient sequence is too opaque.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The central L-value is bridged to a finite-scale smoothed coefficient sum parameterized by analytic conductor. The next representation change is from one hard sum to a family average, where orthogonality may expose cancellation unavailable term by term.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The trivial or average coefficient estimates recover only convexity, and another use of the functional equation does not improve it. A suitable family has not yet been constructed in this unit, so the reduction alone supplies no power saving.
directed.uncertainty: The OCR is unsafe for the exact approximate-functional-equation display, coefficient exponents, and convexity power. The square-root-conductor scale and logical reduction to cancellation are explicit in prose.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Positivity turns a family moment into an individual bound, but the gain is governed by a tension: the family must be rich enough for orthogonality and small enough that isolating one member beats convexity. Shrinking it creates off-diagonal terms that carry the true proof burden.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The method embeds a target form in a family of comparable conductor and estimates a positive moment of their central L-values. Orthogonality and completeness can establish the expected average; positivity then bounds the target by the whole moment. A standard family large enough for diagonal analysis yields only convexity. Subconvexity requires shortening the family, analytically when possible or arithmetically by amplification, and then obtaining new cancellation in the resulting off-diagonal sums.
directed.conceptual_reading: A family converts inaccessible pointwise cancellation into collective structure, while positivity converts collective control back into a pointwise conclusion. The diagonal is the easy coarse contribution; off-diagonal correlation records the information lost when one treats family members as independent.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are a positive family moment, its diagonal/off-diagonal decomposition, and a shortened subfamily. Completeness supplies an averaging identity, positivity isolates the chosen form, and off-diagonal estimates determine whether the shortening is affordable.
directed.boundary_or_failure: A family that is rich but too large recovers only convexity; a short family without control of its off-diagonal terms gives no bound. Analytic shortening exists only in some aspects, motivating amplification in the remaining cases.
directed.uncertainty: Moment formulas, family-size thresholds, and powers of the conductor are OCR-sensitive. The qualitative tradeoff among richness, size, positivity, diagonal analysis, and off-diagonal cost is clearly stated.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The proposed spectral picture uses a multiplication action on an adelic quotient and reads its regularized irreducible decomposition through the explicit formula. The exact prime–zero duality is the mediator, but the construction assumes GRH and therefore interprets zeros rather than proving their location.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source reports Connes's proposal of a singular adelic quotient carrying an action of the idele class group by multiplication. With regularization and assuming GRH, decomposing this action is said to recover the zeros of degree-one automorphic L-functions. The construction is closely tied to Riemann's explicit formula, which equates suitable sums over zeros with sums over primes and prime powers weighted by L-function coefficients; the same formula already serves direct zero-distribution and indirect zero-density arguments.
directed.conceptual_reading: A group action would replace a list of zeros by spectral data of a representation, while the explicit formula acts as a trace-like compatibility condition joining the spectral and prime descriptions. This supplies a candidate meaning for the zeros, not an independent constraint forcing them onto the critical line.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the adelic quotient, idele-class multiplication action, its regularized spectral decomposition, and the explicit formula linking spectral zeros to arithmetic prime powers. Weil's rearrangement is cited as a related function-field-inspired interpretation.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The proposal is conditional on GRH and on a suitable regularization, and the source explicitly says existing zero statistics do not reveal where the natural space or symmetry should be found. It is neither an RH proof nor an established canonical spectral model.
directed.uncertainty: The quotient and action notation are OCR-imperfect, so their exact symbols should be checked against the scan. The conditional status, multiplication-action idea, and explicit-formula connection are clear.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The closing intuition is that a family may constrain zeros more effectively than an isolated spectral model: choose quantities whose averages are accessible and positive, then use their collective incompatibility to exclude hypothetical off-line zeros. A full spectral realization could come before this analysis, but need not logically come first.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The authors judge family methods to be the most successful current way to study zeros and emphasize the choice of averaged quantities together with positivity. They point to the function-field proof, where such family analysis places zeros on the critical line, and imagine two number-field scenarios: family constraints might first rule out fictitious off-line zeros, or a suitable spectral space might first realize the zeros and then be analyzed through families.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proposed move is local-to-global forcing across a family: aggregate positive constraints can make a forbidden local spectral configuration impossible even before each genuine zero has a complete individual interpretation. The alternative sequence separates discovery of the right representation from the analysis that proves purity.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Candidate bridge objects are families of L-functions, deliberately chosen averaged observables, positivity, and eventually a spectral space carrying the zeros. The function-field case supplies the motivating precedent, not a transferred number-field construction.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The authors explicitly call the scenario wild speculation. It gives no candidate average, positivity theorem, spectral space, or proof of GRH, and success over finite fields is not evidence that the same forcing mechanism is available over number fields.
directed.uncertainty: OCR renders the critical-line fraction incorrectly and includes stray layout characters. The two strategic scenarios, their reliance on families and positivity, and their speculative status are unambiguous.
